901.author: yuanzhou75
901.body:
Fixes #900 — the thinking-control half. The image-probe half of #900 is not fixed here and is tracked in #956; unifying the non-stream sender is #958.

When an OpenAI-compatible endpoint returns a 400 that rejects the thinking/reasoning controls the selected variant injects, drop exactly the fields that 400 names and reissue the pre-stream request. Other 400 responses, and requests that have begun streaming, still fail normally.

**What changed**

- **Only a proven rejection counts.** A 400 detail must name a field next to a rejection phrase, or point at it through the provider's own `param`, before anything is stripped. A value complaint such as `thinking budget exceeds max_tokens` fails as sent and suppresses nothing.
- **Strip what was named, remember only what worked.** Each rejection drops only the fields that 400 named, successive per-field 400s accumulate instead of alternating, and the outcome is remembered per endpoint (base URL + model + protocol + variant) only once a stripped request succeeds — a fallback that itself fails cannot downgrade the endpoint.
- **The gateway stops rejecting the probe.** `jiuwenswarm-model-gateway` accepts Swarm's `enable_thinking`/`reasoning` transport keys on tool-less probes; the configured model endpoint stays authoritative for real turns. `Fixes #900` became `Refs #900` because the image half remains.

**Not in this PR:** `completeChatRequest` keeps its "no fallback" contract. Session naming retries the same 400 itself and raises `max_tokens` 64 → 16 384 as part of that retry, so a client-level retry changes when its recovery happens and two of its tests failed in CI. That decision, and the callers that have no recovery at all (paper summaries, the evolution proxy, the Settings connectivity probe), are #958.

**Tests:** `packages/model` 142/142 — a value-complaint 400, a fallback that itself fails, per-field 400s and the `param` pointer; the gateway test covers the accepted probe keys.

906.author: qingkwl
906.body:
First batch of the first-message latency plan (#799): warm the MCP catalog while the user is still on the ready screen, and stop paying a second `skills.list` RPC on every run that imports nothing. Together they address the two largest measured chunks of the first message — the ~48s stdio catalog cold-start (field) and part of the ~4s `skills.list` x3 chain in the SD-side run preparation.

## Warm the MCP catalog right after agent-ready (S1)

On a fresh install the bundled stdio MCP servers spawn and enumerate their tools on the first chat run; field measurements put this chunk at ~48s of the 60-135s first-message latency. The shell's `watchAgentReady` already polls `/agent/info`, and the moment `jiuwenswarm.reachable` turns true it now issues `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload` in the background — the MCP settings page's refresh request, and the one endpoint that actually connects and enumerates. The spawns and tool enumeration then overlap the ready screen instead of the first message.

The endpoint choice was corrected during live verification (commit ef65229e): the first revision fired `GET /api/mcp/sources`, which only reads the cached manifest/status list — on a running stack it answered 200 in ~1s and spawned nothing, and the first chat run still paid the full catalog load. The reload endpoint spawned every bundled source in ~3.3s on the same stack, with the stdio processes visible on the host. Verified locally: catalog warmed at boot → a first message afterwards pays zero MCP chunk (E1.6 evidence pack).

Best-effort by contract: failures are logged to `shell.log` (`[warmup] first-chat /api/mcp/sources/reload -> <status>` or a failure line) and never surface to the user. When the warmup loses the race, the run path re-runs the same steps — no behavioural fork, only a head start.

## One `skills.list` per sync when nothing imports (S3a)

`SkillSync.sync()` ran `skills.list` twice per run: `_sync()` listed to diff staged skills against JiuwenSwarm's, and the tail listed again to refresh the adapter's `directories` map. That map only carries ScienceDiscovery-marked skills, which can only appear through this adapter's own imports — a run that imports nothing changes no directory, so the second listing was the first one's answer. `_sync()` now reports whether it imported anything; `sync()` re-lists only then. The import path is byte-for-byte today's behaviour (pre-import listing + post-import refresh); the steady-state path saves one RPC round trip per run and still populates the map from the single listing, including right after an adapter restart.

This is step S3a of the run-preparation-chain plan; S3c (acceptance-path parallelisation) remains a follow-up.

## One `skills.list` per run, cached 30s with write-through invalidation (S3b)

After S3a a steady-state run still paid two `skills.list` RPCs: `_sync()` listed to diff staged skills, and the API's reconcile listed again through `GET /agent/skills`. Both read the same list, and the adapter performs every write to that list itself (`skills.import_local` in `_import`, `skills.toggle` in `set_enabled`) — so a short-TTL cache with write-through invalidation serves both reads from one fetch while keeping the cached answer at least as fresh as the last write. Back-to-back runs staging the same skills now send **one `skills.list` per run instead of two**; an import or a toggle invalidates immediately, and a zero TTL restores today's fetch-every-read behaviour as the kill switch.

A cache hit never changes what JiuwenSwarm receives: import decisions still run against the freshest answer the adapter itself has written, and a direct JW-side edit can only stay invisible for the 30s TTL — the trade the plan documents. Step S3b of the run-preparation plan.

## Validation

- `pnpm --dir win_desktop build` — clean (esbuild).
- `pnpm --dir win_desktop typecheck` — clean (tsc).
- `pnpm --dir win_desktop test` — 164 pass / 0 fail (5 first-chat-warmup tests: URL/header construction, POST method to the reload endpoint, happy path, failure propagation, timeout bounds; baseline was 159 before this change).
- Live stack check (dev stack, 2026-11-05): `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload` with the shell's auth header returned 200 in ~3.3s and spawned all 13 bundled stdio sources (`ready`); the prior `GET` on the same stack returned 200 in ~1s and spawned nothing — this is what motivated the endpoint fix.
- Adapter: `uv run pytest tests/` (services/adapter) — 292 passed, 1 failed. The failure, `test_diagnostics.py::test_private_rotating_file`, is pre-existing on this host: it fails identically on the unmodified base commit in the same worktree (verified with `git stash`), and the change does not touch diagnostics. All 15 skills tests pass, including 5 that count the RPCs: a no-import sync lists exactly once and still populates the directories map (S3a); an importing sync still lists twice (pre-import + post-import refresh, S3a unchanged); two `listed()` calls within the TTL share one RPC, a no-import sync and the next `listed()` share one RPC (S3b); an import and a toggle each invalidate so the next read re-fetches (S3b); a zero TTL restores fetch-every-read (S3b kill switch).
- Packaged-install validation (2026-11-06, installer built from this branch @ 9679fd28, NSIS 585.6 MB): see journey 5 below. ✅ DONE.
- Local CI layers: `pnpm ci:ut` / `pnpm ci:e2e` cannot run on this host — their sandbox setup needs `bwrap` (bubblewrap), which is Linux-only. Per the workstream's rules this is stated plainly instead of skipped silently; the GitHub Actions runs of the same layers on this PR are the gate (L1 already green, full matrix runs when the draft is marked ready).

## E2E user journeys

**5. Packaged install (the acceptance journey), NSIS `ScienceDiscovery-0.3.0-win-x64-setup.exe` built from this branch @ 9679fd28 (SHA256 57484989EDCAD17A…), Windows 11, quiet load window (2026-11-06):**

| Profile | First message | Second message (same session) | shell.log warmup |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cold first boot | 5.19s | 3.05s | ✅ `2026-11-06T06:16:35Z [warmup] first-chat /api/mcp/sources/reload -> 200` |
| Attach × 3 median | 11.28s | 3.52s | ✅ every boot |
| Real model (J2 OFF baseline) | 20.6s | 18.1s (同会话) | ✅ |
| Real model (J2 ON, progressive) | **15.9s (-23%)** | — | ✅ |

Acceptance vs issue #799 targets: shell warmup fires every boot ✅; warm first message 11.3s ≤ 20s target ✅; second message 3.5s ≪ 8.67s baseline ✅. The cold-first-boot 5.19s on this warm-filesystem machine shows the mechanism (catalog already hot when the user types); the field cold-install number (≈48s catalog tax) is what S1 eliminates — that is the mechanism journey 3 already proves on the dev tree. J2 (progressive tools) is upstream behaviour — measured here only for cross-reference; this PR does not change it (the -23% first-message figure is the evidence the separate J2 upstream proposal will cite). PASS.

Local stack (dev tree, base 79d26dd6 + this branch), mock OpenAI endpoint on loopback answering SSE in ~30 ms, quiet load window, same-window pairs (D5 discipline: fresh session first message vs same-session second, median of 3):

1. **Warmup fires end-to-end (the S1 claim).** Desktop shell launched against the live stack; `shell.log` recorded `[warmup] first-chat /api/mcp/sources/reload -> 200`, and the API log recorded `mcp_catalog_loaded durationMs=3846 failedServerCount=0 serverCount=3 toolCount=39` in the same second. The 6 bundled stdio MCP server processes were visible on the host before any message was sent. PASS.
2. **First/second message, web-only connectors (E1 anatomy口径).** First message 5.5s / 9.4s / (one round lost to a transient Windows file-lock EPERM, retried clean) — median ≈ 5.5-9.4s; second message 3.5s median. The 2026-11-03 baseline on the old base was 26.09s / 8.67s; the drop is mostly upstream work landed in the meantime (patch 0020 moved the 12.4s observability import off the hot-start path) plus the quiet load window — this pair is reported as no-regression evidence, not as S1/S3a attribution. PASS (no regression).
3. **First message with an MCP tool call, cold vs warm catalog (the S1 mechanism).** Session with `enabledConnectorIds: ["web","uniprot"]`, mock model answers the prompt with one `mcp__uniprot__search` call. Cold catalog (API boot refresh had failed: `mcp_connection_failed … MCP connection timeout` × 3 servers at startup, as it does on this host): run completed in ~7.7s with the catalog load inside the run. Warm catalog (after `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload`, the exact S1 request): run completed in 5.7s, tool call answered in 16ms, no connection events in the run window. Delta ≈ 2s on this warm-filesystem dev box; the field cold-install figure the plan cites is ~48s (E1.6 evidence). PASS — the warmup demonstrably moves the catalog load out of the first run.
4. **S3a mechanism.** Adapter unit tests count the RPCs directly (a no-import sync sends exactly one `skills.list`, an importing sync still sends two); the dev-stack venv still runs the pre-S3a adapter build, so the in-stack numbers above are the conservative (two-list) path. PASS by unit test; in-stack A/B lands when the venv is refreshed.

Failure attribution: the only run failures in the session were transient host file-lock EPERMs on skill-snapshot rename (Windows antivirus/indexer) — retried clean, not product failures. The pre-existing `test_private_rotating_file` failure is documented in Validation above.

Commands: `node .tmp/mock-openai.mjs` (mock, SSE instant), `node .tmp/fml-ab.mjs 3` and `node .tmp/fml-s1-ab.mjs cold|warm` (drivers; client-side SSE timing + event timeline). Counts: journey 1 = 1/1 PASS; journey 2 = 5/6 runs clean (1 env-retry); journey 3 = 1/1 cold + 1/1 warm PASS; journey 4 = 10/10 unit tests; journey 5 = packaged NSIS validation (cold/attach/real-model J2 OFF/ON, 2026-11-06).

## Release

Release category: `release:performance` (GitHub label pending a maintainer — the author has read-only access to the upstream repository and cannot apply it).
User impact: faster first message on installed builds (the MCP catalog no longer cold-starts inside the first chat run) and slightly cheaper every run (one fewer `skills.list` round trip in the steady state). No UI change, no configuration change, no behaviour change on failure paths.
Compatibility and migration: none.

908.author: HugoXK
908.body:
Fixes #884

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## What is wrong

`GET /api/sessions/:session/artifact-versions/:version/diff` answered **500 `Internal server error`** when either version of the pair is not textual, and logged a false `unclassified_request_error`. `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts:357` threw a plain `Error("Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions")`, whose prose matches no client-input pattern in `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` and no not-found mapper in `services/api/src/http/index.ts`, so the top-level catch classified a client-input problem as a server fault.

Measured at `7057aaf6` with two `application/zip` versions of one artifact in one session (red commit `0be111de` only):

```
GET /api/sessions/<id>/artifact-versions/<version>/diff
500 {"error":"Internal server error"}
```

The same request, with logging configured the way `startPlatform` does (not by `createApiServer` alone), wrote:

```
ERROR [api] event=unclassified_request_error errorMessage="Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions" method=GET path=/api/sessions/<id>/artifact-versions/<version>/diff status=500
```

## The fix — option 2 from the issue, in the helper

`artifactVersionDiff` now throws `new ApiStatusError(400, "Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions")`. The rejection is classified by **class** (the top-level catch answers `ApiStatusError.statusCode` before any prose matching), and it sits where the rule lives, so every caller of the helper answers the same 400 instead of only this route. No new message pattern was added to `isKnownClientInputError`.

The versions both exist; this is not a missing resource, which is why it is a 400 and not the 404 family `#881` adds.

### Why the route was not touched (overlap with #881)

`#881` (ours, open) rewrites the `diff` route block in `services/api/src/http/index.ts` for the missing-`to` / missing-`against` cases. Hoisting the media-type check into that same block would (a) collide textually with `#881`, and (b) put the from-version resolution in two places: the route would have to repeat what the helper already computes, and the next caller of the helper would get the 500 again. This fix touches only `services/api/src/artifacts/index.ts`; the two behaviours are complementary (`#881` = missing version, this = both present but not comparable), so whichever lands second keeps both without a conflict.

### Import note

`services/api/src/runs/index.ts` already imports `artifacts/index.ts`, so importing `ApiStatusError` from `runs` inside `artifacts` would have closed a cycle between two large modules. The class therefore lives in `services/api/src/http/api-status-error.ts`, which imports nothing; `runs/index.ts` imports it and re-exports it (its public API is unchanged, so the existing import in `services/api/src/http/index.ts` still works), and `artifacts/index.ts` imports the leaf directly. No reverse edge was added and no cycle exists.

The leaf move keeps the identity check honest: `services/api/src/http/index.ts` still matches `error instanceof ApiStatusError` against the class the helper throws, which the new test proves by driving that exact path — a divergent class object would answer 500, not the 400 asserted there.

## Red → green

`services/api/src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts` (test-only commit `0be111de`) seeds versions through `SessionStore.createArtifactVersion` and asks the real route, so no execution is driven: an `application/zip` pair, a pair that switches from `text/markdown` to `application/zip`, and a `text/markdown` control pair that must keep diffing.

Red at `7057aaf6`:

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts
not ok 1 - a non-textual artifact pair answers a client error instead of 500
  error: |-
    binary pair must answer 400 with the reason, not 500
      body: { error: 'Internal server error' }
      status: 500
# tests 1 / # pass 0 / # fail 1
```

Green at `207243a7` (same command): `1 test / 1 pass / 0 fail`, exit 0. That run was still green by luck — see the review fix below.

The false log is gone in the same manual repro: `STATUS 400 {"error":"Diff is available only for textual or comparable artifact versions"}`, `grep -c unclassified_request_error` → `0`, and the request is logged as `http_request_failed … statusCode=400`.

## Review fix — the fixture seeded after the server's `ready` chain

`sciencediscovery-bot`'s thread on `artifact-version-diff-media.test.ts:130` is right and this is a test-only correction: `createApiServer` returns before `ready` (which ends in `store.load()`) has run, and the fixture seeded after `server.listen`, so the test passed only when the seeds landed before that load. Two commits, no product code changed:

- `b3eb58b8` makes the ordering explicit: a request settles `ready` before the seeds. It is red, deterministically, on a machine that starts the server quickly:
  ```
  not ok 1 - a non-textual artifact pair answers a client error instead of 500
      binary pair must answer 400 with the reason, not 500
      +     error: 'Internal server error'
      +   status: 500
  ```
  (the 500 is the pre-fix behaviour: the route's `store` has already loaded a catalog without these versions, `getArtifactVersion` returns `undefined`, and `artifacts/index.ts` throws the plain `Error("Artifact version not found")`.)
- `76e911b5` removes the race instead of winning it: `startHttpFixture` is split into `createFixture` + `startHttpServer(context, fixture)`, the test writes every version first and starts the server afterwards, so `ready` loads a catalog that already contains them. No wait, retry or timeout is involved.

Green five consecutive runs of the same command, one process each:

```
[run 1] # pass 1 # fail 0
[run 2] # pass 1 # fail 0

913.author: ink999107
913.body:
`search_preprints` asked the provider for `/{days}d/0/json`. bioRxiv and medRxiv answer that request with HTTP 200, an empty `collection`, and a "Both dates must be in yyyy-mm-dd format" message, so the gateway read a rejected request as "no matches" and the assistant told users the window contained no preprints.

## Dated-range requests

`config/external-urls.json` now carries a `yyy-mm-dd` range template instead of the invalid `{days}d` form, and `_preprint_search` computes the window in UTC (`days=1` yields a single-day range). UTC avoids "today" landing in the provider's future.

## Provider failures are no longer silent

A `messages[0].status` that reports a rejected request now raises instead of returning a clean empty result. Invalid requests still return HTTP 200, so this status message is the only failure signal the provider gives.

An empty window is not a rejection: the provider answers one with its own status, `no posts found`, and no `total`. That status is accepted and mapped onto the existing empty-window warning — "The provider reports no preprints published between …" — so a `days=1` search on a quiet day, or a category with nothing in the window, returns an empty result rather than a tool error.

## Newest-first scanning within the tool deadline

The provider serves a window oldest-first, and its trailing path segment is a record offset, not a page number: measured on both servers, cursor 1 starts one record after cursor 0, so adjacent cursors share 29 of 30 records. The search starts at the newest offset and walks backwards, dedupes DOIs that shift between pages while the window moves, and reports how much of the window it actually scanned. Previously the warning implied the whole window had been filtered.

The walk has to fit the 30 s deadline that the Node MCP transport gives a search tool call, so it spends a wall-clock budget rather than counting pages:

- one HTTP client for the whole scan, so pages reuse the connection instead of paying a TLS handshake each;
- every request on this path, the first page included, is bounded by the same deadline;
- the newest page alone first, because it usually fills `limit`, then up to four pages in flight;
- a 20 s stop, leaving headroom for the answer to return, with the warning saying the scan stopped early;
- each page gets the budget that is left, so a slow page costs that page and not the
  pages of its batch that already answered;
- one reconnect when the provider closes an idle keep-alive connection between pages.

The page fetched to learn `total` (offset 0) is reused as the tail of the walk instead of being downloaded and discarded; coverage counts distinct offsets, so the reused tail is not reported twice.

## Validation

- Gateway suite: 43 tests, 43 passed, 0 failed.
  `PYTHONPATH=services/gateway/src python -m unittest discover -s services/gateway/tests -p 'test_*.py'`
  (run from the branch head with the service virtualenv because workspace dependency preparation could not complete in this environment — see below).
- L1 slice on this head: planned 4, executed 4, passed 4, failed 0, skipped 0.
- Live provider smoke, no mocks:
  - Empty window: bioRxiv `liver`, 1 day, `category=zoology` → 0 records, warning "The provider reports no preprints published between 2026-11-05 to 2026-11-05", answered in 2.5 s. Before this round the same call raised.
  - medRxiv `diabetes`, 30 days, limit 3 → 2 records from the newest page, "Scanned 30 of 1873 … stopped at its 20-second time budget". The host used for this smoke fetched 6–9 s per page at the time, so the budget, not the scan design, ended it.
  - bioRxiv `liver`, 30 days, limit 5 → "Scanned 30 of 7257", stopped at the time budget, 0 records from that page; the same query returned 5 records when the host's per-page latency was under 2 s.
  - `lookup_doi` for a returned bioRxiv DOI: still returns its versions (no regression).
- Not run locally: UT, ST and E2E. The shared runner's preparation (`uv sync`) stalls downloading dependency wheels from the PyPI CDN at roughly 20 KB/s in this environment; switching to a mirror conflicts with the committed lockfile. No assertion was weakened or skipped to work around it. The gateway suite above exercises the changed code, and CI runs the full layers on this head.

## E2E user journeys

BLOCKED: the mocked browser E2E layer was not run for the reason above. The affected path is an MCP tool invoked by the assistant rather than a browser journey; the live provider smoke in Validation is the substitute evidence for it. Tested SHA: ec7b75d6.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: bioRxiv and medRxiv searches return matching recent preprints instead of an always-empty list; a rejected provider request surfaces as an error rather than as "no results"; an empty date window stays an empty result. The tool warning now states how much of the date window was scanned and whether the scan stopped early.

Compatibility and migration: the configuration key `data_sources.preprints.details_by_days_template` is replaced by `data_sources.preprints.details_by_range_template`; a deployment that uses a customized copy of `config/external-urls.json` must apply the same rename. Running gateway processes must be restarted because the URL table is cached in-process.

Labels: `release:fix`, `bug` and `bot-reviewed` are applied.

915.body:
Fixes #914

Owner: Dev-2
Written-by: Dev-2

## Problem

`UT` on PR #890 (tip `fdb835fb`, run `42015883088`, job `127206585414`) failed `services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py::ArchitectureBoundaryTests::test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names` with a `FileNotFoundError` instead of an assertion:

```
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
'.../services/api/.tmp/agent-skill-creator-1793877061398-12103/projects/.../skill-snapshots/.716ffbc5-....skill-snapshot/antibody-design/scripts/install_pipeline_deps.sh'
```

The UT layer read `planned 6366 / executed 6366 / passed 6365 / failed 1 / skipped 0`; the group holding it was `1 failed, 30 passed in 4.55s` (the other 30 gateway Python tests ran normally). The same test set was green on the previous tip of that branch (`c4fb33d4`, run `41890794011`), and the failing PR's diff touches neither `services/gateway` nor `services/api/.tmp`.

## Cause

`_files()` walks `services/api`, `packages`, `apps/web` and `test/api` and skips only `__pycache__`, `dist`, `node_modules`. `services/api/.tmp` is a live runtime workspace root, not source: `services/api/src/server.test.ts` and the skill-creator paths create session trees there while other workers run and delete them after. The walk lists a path, the owning test removes it, `read_text()` raises, and the boundary assertion is replaced by an error that has nothing to do with the pull request's diff. The cost is a full CI cycle plus a rerun that we cannot trigger ourselves.

## Red first

Two deterministic regression tests at `7057aaf6` (test commit `1c7817a2`). Both create their probe under `services/api/.tmp` and remove it in cleanup:

```
FAILED services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py::GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests::test_a_workspace_file_removed_after_listing_is_skipped
E   FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../services/api/.tmp/probe-boundary-3.ts'

FAILED services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py::GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests::test_a_generated_workspace_is_not_walked
E   AssertionError: 'content: services/api/.tmp/probe-boundary-3.ts' unexpectedly found in ['content: services/api/.tmp/probe-boundary-3.ts']

2 failed, 3 passed, 1 warning in 7.71s
```

The first reproduces the CI shape exactly without relying on timing: the listing yields a path that is already gone when the walk reads it. The second is the `.tmp` root itself being walked as source. Both fail on `main` and pass after the fix.

## After fix

Two changes, one file:

- `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` gains `.tmp`: like `dist`, it is generated runtime data, not source.
- The read side treats `FileNotFoundError` as "the file vanished after the listing" and skips that path: a source file removed mid-walk cannot be asserted on, and an assertion is not what we want to raise here.

```
$ python3 -m pytest services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py -q
5 passed, 1 warning in 3.93s
```

`git diff --stat 7057aaf6..HEAD`: 1 file, `+69/−13` (`services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py`). `_node_boundary_failures()` is the walk extracted from the existing test so both the original assertion and the regression tests exercise the same code path.

Not run: the full `services/gateway/tests` suite and CI; this file is the gate for this issue.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: none for users; a CI layer no longer fails on unrelated pull requests when an API test deletes its temporary workspace while the architecture-boundary walk is reading it.
Compatibility and migration: none.

922.author: HugoXK
922.body:
Fixes #665

`web_fetch`'s public-URL guard lets several IPv6 families through even though each one carries an IPv4 address the guard already knows how to judge. A model-supplied URL such as `http://[64:ff9b::7f00:1]/` or `http://[2002:a9fe:a9fe::]/` reaches loopback or the link-local metadata endpoint, while the equivalent `::ffff:127.0.0.1` is rejected. This closes those holes, pins that public addresses in the same forms keep working, and — after review — refuses the non-canonical suffixes of the local-use NAT64 prefix rather than guessing where their IPv4 address sits.

## What was wrong

`ipv6Blocked()` consulted `ipv4Blocked()` only for IPv4-mapped (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) and IPv4-compatible (`::a.b.c.d`) forms, where the embedded IPv4 address sits in the last two hextets. Other families carry the same address elsewhere:

| family | prefix | where the IPv4 address sits | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NAT64 well-known | `64:ff9b::/96` | last 32 bits | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| NAT64 local-use | `64:ff9b:1::/48` | last 32 bits **only for the canonical `/96` sub-layout** | canonical `/96` decoded; every other suffix under the `/48` rejected |
| 6to4 | `2002::/16` | hextets 2–3 | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| IPv4-translated | `::ffff:0:0:0/96` | last 32 bits, after `ffff` and 16 zero bits | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| Teredo | `2001:0::/32` | last 32 bits, bitwise inverted | decode, then `ipv4Blocked` |
| site-local (deprecated) | `fec0::/10` | no IPv4 — the range itself is non-public | reject |

No branch inspected those positions, so each form fell through to `return false`.

The local-use row is the review fix. `64:ff9b:1::/48` is wider than the `/96` an embedded address needs, and RFC 8215 allows deployments to use other suffix lengths — a deployment that puts the IPv4 address in bits 64–95 is not judged by hextets 6–7. Reading hextets 6–7 of *every* address in the `/48` therefore judged the wrong bits: `64:ff9b:1:0:7f00:1:808:808` was interpreted as the public `128.8.8.8`.

## What changed

`packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts`: one helper, `dotted(high, low)`, and `ipv6Blocked()` extracts the embedded address for the rows above and hands it to the existing `ipv4Blocked()`. There is no second copy of the IPv4 block list, no blanket range ban, and no refactor of the existing mapped/compatible branches.

For the local-use prefix the rule is now explicit and fail-closed: decode the canonical `64:ff9b:1:0:0:0::/96` sub-layout, and **return blocked for every non-canonical suffix** under `64:ff9b:1::/48` (`return true`, never `return false` — an unknown suffix must not become the way around the guard). The well-known `64:ff9b::/96` prefix is untouched by that rule.

## Red first

The new test (`providers.test.ts`), run against the unfixed `url-guard.ts`:

```
not ok 11 - web_fetch judges NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local literals by their embedded IPv4
  error: |-
    64:ff9b:1:0:7f00:1:808:808

    false !== true

  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
  expected: true
  actual: false
# tests 16
# pass 15
# fail 1
```

The assertion loop stops at its first failing literal, so every blocked literal was also probed one by one against the unfixed predicate, and every public one against the fixed predicate. Values are `blocked` / `allowed` from `isBlockedAddress`; the flipped rows are the review fix, all in the tightening direction:

| address | before `e9e7358c` review fix | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `64:ff9b::7f00:1` | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b::808:808` | allowed | allowed |
| `64:ff9b:1::7f00:1` (canonical `/96`) | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1::a9fe:a9fe` (canonical `/96`) | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1::808:808` (canonical `/96`) | allowed | allowed |
| `64:ff9b:1:1:0:0:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:0:1:0:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:0:0:1:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:dead:beef:cafe:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:1:0:0:7f00:1` | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:1:0:0:a9fe:a9fe` | blocked | blocked |
| `64:ff9b:1:0:7f00:1:808:808` | **allowed** | blocked |

Five flips in this probed set, all `allowed → blocked`; zero `blocked → allowed`.

## Only tighter

The same probe run before and after the review fix differs in exactly one line — the tightened address. Everything a legitimate client may reach still resolves as public:

```
ALLOW  literal 64:ff9b::808:808            (NAT64 well-known, public)
ALLOW  literal 64:ff9b:1::808:808          (NAT64 local-use canonical /96, public)
ALLOW  literal 2002:808:808::              (6to4 for 8.8.8.8)
ALLOW  literal ::ffff:0:808:808            (IPv4-translated for 8.8.8.8)
ALLOW  literal 2001:0:808:808::f7f7:f7f7   (Teredo for 8.8.8.8)
ALLOW  literal 2606:4700:4700::1111        (native IPv6)
ALLOW  resolver 64:ff9b::808:808 for http://example.com/
ALLOW  resolver 2606:4700:4700::1111 for http://example.com/
```

These are asserted in the test too (`assert.equal(isBlockedAddress(...), false)` and `assert.equal(await assertPublicUrl(...), url)`), so the guard cannot be "fixed" by blocking a prefix.

## After the fix

```
# tests 16
# pass 16
# fail 0
```

The test now has 17 blocked addresses and 6 public ones (23 assertions across the literal and resolver paths), including the canonical `/96` cases in both directions and the non-canonical suffixes.

Diffstat against `main` `f4dd1813`:

```
 packages/data-source/src/web/native/providers.test.ts | 71 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts      | 35 +++++++++++-
 2 files changed, 106 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)
```

This branch is `f4dd1813` + four commits, two files, nothing else:

1. `dd29d921` test: pin NAT64, 6to4, IPv4-translated and site-local fetch targets
2. `eb818998` fix: judge NAT64, 6to4 and IPv4-translated literals by their embedded IPv4
3. `e4bb3e67` test: judge the local-use NAT64 prefix by its canonical /96 only
4. `e9e7358c` fix: decode only the canonical /96 under the local-use NAT64 prefix

It does not contain any commit from #915; the three-file view was the reviewer's worktree.

Ran:
- `node --import tsx --test src/web/native/providers.test.ts` in `packages/data-source` — `# tests 16 # pass 16 # fail 0`; the same command on the unfixed source is the red above (`# pass 15 # fail 1`).

- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.

924.body:
Fixes #839

A delimited dataset preview derived one number, `Math.max(header.length, widest)`, and used it for two jobs: the grid width and the column count it reported. A two-column `.csv` with one 200,001-field line rendered 1,001 mostly-blank columns and announced `The file has 200001 columns; the preview shows the first 1001.` Both halves now come from the header: the column count *is* the header, and a wider line may add only a small, capped set of unnamed surplus columns.

## What was wrong

- **The count.** `clippedColumns.total` was `Math.max(header.length, widest)` — a data line's field count presented as the file's schema. The only sentence the reader gets was built from it, so a two-column file was described as a 200,001-column one, and the same outlier cells were named twice ("has N columns" and "M cells past the preview width").

- **The width.** `width = min(totalColumns, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)`, so one outlier line decided how wide the grid was. Taking the width from the *returned* rows instead would make the column set depend on the client's `maxRows` (the previous defect), so neither end of the file may own the width.

## What changed

`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts`, `parseDelimitedTable` only:

- `totalColumns = header.length` — the header is the schema; a wide row is a row.
- `surplusLimit = Math.min(16, Math.max(2, header.length))` — the cap `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts` already uses (`surplusColumnLimit`). A wider line may contribute at most that many **unnamed** surplus columns; a header at or past sixteen keeps every named column (`surplusLimit` only ever adds).
- `width = Math.min(header.length + surplusShown, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)`, where `surplusShown = min(widest - header.length, surplusLimit)` — `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS` stays the absolute payload limit.
- `clippedColumns = { shown: Math.min(header.length, width), total: header.length }` — `shown` is the number of named columns the preview shows, so it is consistent with the new width and never exceeds the header. The column sentence therefore fires only when the header itself is wider than the preview.
- Cells past the width still go to `clippedCells`; a header wider than the payload cap is still reported through `clippedColumns`, exactly as before.
- A line past the row window may still set the width — the column set must not depend on the caller's `maxRows` — and the returned rows are padded to it, as before. What changes is that the padding is no longer silent: `paddingOnlyColumns = surplusShown - shownSurplus` (the surplus only an unseen line justifies) and `paddingOnlyCells = paddingOnlyColumns * rows.length` produce `The preview pads N unnamed columns (M blank cells) because the file has a wider line past the first K rows, which is not shown.` `clippedCells` keeps counting only returned rows' cells past the width, and a returned outlier produces no padding sentence.

Measured on the fixtures (all asserted in `services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts`):

| fixture | columns | clipped | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2-column header + one 200,001-field line inside the window | `4` | `clippedCells 199997` | issue fixture: was 1,001 columns |
| 2-column header, no outlier | `2` | `clippedCells 0` | a narrow table is not widened to the cap |
| 8-column header + one 100-field line | `16` | `clippedCells 84` | header + capped surplus |
| 20-column header + one 200,001-field line | `36` | `clippedCells 199965`, all 20 names in order | the cap never takes a named column |
| 200,001-column header | `1001` | `clippedColumns {shown: 1001, total: 200001}` | `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS` still the absolute limit |

## Red first — the column count

The new count test run against the unfixed `parseDelimitedTable`, with the two stale assertions in `dashboard.test.ts` already corrected (the tree a reviewer replays with the test commit):

```
not ok 62 - a delimited preview caps a pathological line and counts what it leaves out
  error: |-
    the column count comes from the header; the wide row is cells, not columns
    + actual - expected
      { shown: 1001, + total: 200001 - total: 2 }

not ok 63 - a wide line past the row window does not become the file's column count
  error: |-
    the file has as many columns as its header

    5000 !== 2

# tests 67
# pass 65
# fail 2
```

## Red first — the width

The width assertions run against the same unfixed source (the final tree of this PR's tests):

```
not ok 62 - a delimited preview caps a pathological line and counts what it leaves out
    1001 !== 4
not ok 63 - a wide line past the row window does not become the file's column count
    1001 !== 4
not ok 64 - the surplus cap never takes a named column and scales with the header
    1001 !== 36
not ok 66 - a delimited preview shows the same columns whatever maxRows it is asked for
    1001 !== 4

# tests 68
# pass 64
# fail 4
```

## Red first — padding from a line past the row window

`agent-ci-infra-bot`'s F1: a file whose only wide line falls past the row window still widens the grid, and the payload said nothing about it (`clippedCells 0`, `warnings []`). Pinned in `621c3dcf` before any source change; fixture `a,b` + 100 x `1,2` + one 5,000-field line, so the grid is 4 columns and the outlier is row 101:

```
not ok 63 - a wide line past the row window does not become the file's column count
  error: |-
    the padding of an out-of-window line needs a warning of its own: []

    0 !== 1

# tests 68
# pass 67
# fail 1
```

The same test now also carries the in-window control: an outlier the preview does return is still counted as 4,996 cells past the width (`clippedCells`), and it must not produce the padding sentence.

## Red first — the padding count under the column cap

`agent-ci-infra-bot`'s next finding: the sentence assumed the grid is `header + surplusShown`, but `width` is `Math.min(header + surplusShown, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)`, so a wide header makes it claim unnamed columns the grid does not hold. Pinned in `921ec1d4` before any source change:

```
not ok 64 - the padding sentence counts the unnamed columns the capped grid really holds
  error: |-
    the capped grid has no unnamed column, so there is nothing to report as padding
    + [
    +   'The preview pads 15 unnamed columns (1500 blank cells) because the file has a wider line past the first 100 rows, which is not shown.'
    + ]
    - []

not ok 65 - the padding sentence names the row window it is talking about
  error: 'the sentence counts rows, singular: The preview pads 2 unnamed columns (2 blank cells) because the file has a wider line past the first 1 rows, which is not shown.'

# tests 70
# pass 68
# fail 2
```

The fix counts from the grid that was actually built (`renderedSurplus = max(0, width - totalColumns)`), so a 1,001-column header with a hidden 1,016-field line reports no padding at all, and a 1,000-column header reports exactly the one unnamed column the cap leaves room for.

## After the fix — readings

```
# tests 70
# pass 70
# fail 0
```

Payload readings on the F1 fixture (`a,b` + 100 x `1,2` + one 5,000-field line, so the only wide line is row 101 and is never returned): `columns.length 4`, `clippedColumns {shown: 2, total: 2}`, `clippedCells 0`, and one warning — `The preview pads 2 unnamed columns (200 blank cells) because the file has a wider line past the first 100 rows, which is not shown.` The in-window control in the same test returns that outlier instead: `clippedCells 4996`, no padding sentence.

Diffstat against `main` `f4dd1813`:

```
 services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts |  51 ++++++-
 services/api/src/dashboard.test.ts     | 258 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++--
 2 files changed, 293 insertions(+), 16 deletions(-)
```

Commits (test → fix, twice):

1. `2d8a9835` test: pin a delimited preview's column count to its header
2. `8a78ef4a` fix: take a delimited preview's column count from its header
3. `5575361e` test: cap the unnamed surplus, never the header's own columns
4. `4c4cd346` fix: cap only the unnamed surplus columns of a delimited preview
5. `c562503b` test: pin a narrow two-column table and a twenty-column header
6. `621c3dcf` test: pin that padding from a line past the row window is reported
7. `b807482b` fix: report the padding a line past the row window adds
8. `921ec1d4` test: pin that the padding sentence matches the capped grid
9. `913da859` fix: count the padding from the grid the cap actually builds

Ran:
- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/dashboard.test.ts` — `# tests 70 # pass 70 # fail 0`; the same file against the unfixed source is the four red blocks above (`# pass 65`, `# pass 64`, `# pass 67`, `# pass 68`).
- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.

Not run:
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api test` (the whole api suite) and the `ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e` layers were not run locally on this branch; CI runs them on this pull request.
- No browser journey: the rendered `DatasetTable` shows the payload's `columns` / `warnings` verbatim, and those are what the assertions pin.

## Payload semantics

`clippedColumns` is part of the preview payload, so this changes what one of its fields counts — it is not only an extra sentence:

| field | before this PR | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clippedColumns.total` | `Math.max(header.length, widest)` — a data line's field count | `header.length` — the header is the schema |
| `clippedColumns.shown` | `Math.min(total, width)` | `Math.min(header.length, width)`, so `shown <= total` holds again |
| `columns.length` vs `clippedColumns.total` | equal | `columns.length` may exceed `total` by up to `surplusLimit` unnamed surplus columns |
| `clippedCells` | cells of returned rows past the width | unchanged |
| `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS` | 1,001 | unchanged |

A consumer that read `clippedColumns.total` as "the file's column count" now gets the header's count, which is the schema #839 asked for. The unnamed surplus is the `columns.length - clippedColumns.total` gap, and `warnings` names it when an unseen line is the reason. `apps/web`'s `DatasetTable` renders `columns`, `clippedColumns` and `clippedCells`; it does not render `warnings` today, so the new sentence reaches the API payload only. Showing it in the table (with a localized sentence) is a separate `apps/web` follow-up, not part of this PR.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: a delimited preview no longer renders hundreds of blank columns because of one outlier line, and no longer tells the reader a column count the header does not have. A header wider than the payload cap still gets its explicit clipped-column signal.

Compatibility and migration: none. The payload shape is unchanged; `clippedColumns.total` now counts header columns, `clippedColumns.shown` counts the named columns shown, and the grid width is bounded by header + capped surplus.

Under zh-CN — the product default — the Session activity panel prints the two values it takes from

## Cause

`apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx` rendered `item.state` / `item.provenance` straight into the
tree, and `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` carried the 25 `activity.*` chrome keys but no keys for
those two value domains. Every other surface already translates them (`WakeNotice.tsx` maps wake
states through `chat.wakeNoticeState.*`, `GovernedDownloadCards.tsx` does the same for downloads);
this was the one activity surface left in English.

## Change

Product: two files, +51/−8.

- `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` — `activity.state.{queued,running,completed,failed,cancelled,unknown}`

  carry. Used in the three badge children (executions, transfers, reminders), the three
  `ProcessRecord` labels and the `executionMeta` call.

Untouched by design: the `activity-badge ${item.state}` class (styling keys on it), `live` /
`cancellable`, the `progress.length` accounting, and every other badge in the app. A transfer's
`partial`, a reminder's `fired` and provenance `unconfirmed` are out of scope and keep their raw
token: the state fallback is asserted (`paused` keeps its token), while `unconfirmed` provenance
appears in the fixture and keeps its token by the same lookup, without a dedicated assertion.

Test: `apps/web/tests/AgentActivityPanel.test.tsx`, +38 — one new case, no assertion migration in

Two mocked journeys asserted the raw token as visible text and now assert the sentence a reader
gets (+6/−3, test-only): `test/issue-85-foreground-exec-inbox.spec.ts` asserts `已完成` and keeps

- `test/issue-85-foreground-exec-inbox.spec.ts:274` — expected substring `completed`, received

- `test/journey-execution-management.spec.ts:88` (and `:90`) — expected substring `cancelled`,

The new case also pins both boundaries: an unknown state keeps its raw token
(`activity-badge paused` → `paused`, asserted), and `unconfirmed` provenance is a fixture value with

Pending` — the eight existing cases (English chrome: `View logs`, `Cancel execution`, `Resume …`)

Fixes #923

`PUT /api/web/settings` answers 500 `{"error":"Internal server error"}` when a caller sends a value `normalizeWebSettings` rejects, so the client is told the server broke instead of which field it got wrong. Two of the three user-facing rejections in that function were plain `Error`s whose prose the request classifier does not recognise, so they fell through to the catch-all and were logged as server faults.

## What was wrong

- `services/api/src/store/settings.ts` throws `Error("Unsupported web fetch provider")` and `` Error(`Unknown web setting: ${unknown}`) `` — neither matches the eight prose patterns in `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts`, which is why `deepseekEnabled must be a boolean` already answered 400 and these two answered 500.
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts:1255` calls `store.updateWebSettings(await readJson(...))` with no local mapping, so both reach the shared chain and its `unclassified_request_error` branch.

## What changed

- Both rejections now carry `code: "INVALID_WEB_SETTINGS"` (`Object.assign(new Error(message), { code })`, the same shape `workspace-upload.ts` uses for `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`).
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts` gets one dispatch line next to the existing `SKILL_LIBRARY_VALIDATION` branch: `else if (code === "INVALID_WEB_SETTINGS") sendError(response, 400, message);`.
- No `SessionStoreHttpError` import in `store/settings.ts`: `services/api/src/store.ts` already imports `normalizeWebSettings` from that module, so the reverse import would create a cycle (the reason #884's review rejected the same shape). No new prose pattern either; the stable code is what the classifier's own header asks for.
- Nothing else in the dispatch chain is touched — the artifact-version 404 branch that #881 edits is untouched, and that is the only overlap between the two branches.

## Red first

`services/api/src/web-settings-api.test.ts` starts a real `createApiServer` (offline MCP transport) and sends the request over HTTP. Against the unfixed dispatcher:

```
not ok 1 - an unsupported fetch provider is a 400 that names it, not a 500
  error: |-
    an unsupported provider is client input, not a server fault

    500 !== 400

not ok 2 - an unknown setting key is a 400 that names the key
  error: |-
    an unrecognised key is client input, not a server fault

    500 !== 400

# tests 3
# pass 1
# fail 2
```

The third case (valid `PUT`, then `GET` read-back) passed before the change, which is what pins the route and its auth as healthy.

## After the fix

```
# tests 3
# pass 3
# fail 0
```

- `PUT {"fetchProvider":"definitely-not-a-provider"}` → 400 `{"error":"Unsupported web fetch provider"}`, and no `unclassified_request_error` appears in the server log (checked by grepping the run's output: 0 matches).
- `PUT {"nope":1}` → 400 `{"error":"Unknown web setting: nope"}`.
- `PUT {"searchCacheTtlSeconds":17}` → 200, then `GET` → 200 with `searchCacheTtlSeconds: 17`, so an accepted value is persisted, not merely echoed.

```

- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `node --import tsx --test src/store.test.ts` — `# tests 121 # pass 121 # fail 0` (the store's own settings tests still pass with the coded rejection).

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

Deleting a model currently fails when sessions or runtime defaults reference it. This change allows deleting models and providers while retaining historical sessions, messages, and run snapshots, and makes Web and Desktop agree on the saved model selection after reloads.

Refs #845.

## Behavior

- Delete a referenced model or provider without deleting its sessions. If it owns the global task-model default, the confirmation lets the user choose a replacement or leave the default unset. Removal, defaults, compatibility mirrors, and encrypted-secret cleanup commit atomically. A stale confirmation cannot overwrite a newer global default.
- Preserve an explicitly selected, deleted model in session overrides as unavailable, including across API restarts. It blocks inherited fallback until the user selects another model or clears that override. Session compatibility fields reflect the effective selection; historical runs retain their original snapshots.
- Clear deleted global/project default references. Sessions without explicit model overrides follow the remaining project/global inheritance rules. Editing an existing profile does not reclaim a deliberately cleared global default; adding a model retains the existing setup behavior that fills an unset default.
- Use the direct model picker to recover a Web session. Desktop restores the server selection, honors project defaults for new drafts, and keeps history accessible after the last model is removed. Visible frontends refresh model settings every five seconds and on focus without polling message histories.
- Return a structured `SESSION_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` error before starting a run, and handle run-creation failures in the CLI. Update existing browser deletion journeys for the new confirmation and default-clearing contract.

Fixes #910

Classification: **hygiene, not a product fix.** Test-only change to `source-health.test.ts`; product behaviour is unchanged. Excluded from sprint window scoring and today's KPI on the Lead's ruling.

The harm is real but indirect: the injected-fault wait timing out turns `UT` red for pull requests that do not touch `packages/data-source` at all. `#872` hit exactly this (`NODE_HOOK_OR_COLLECTION_FAILED: packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts`, `planned 6279 / failed 1`) although all four of its changed files are under `apps/web`. That is a false red, not a defect in the code under test.

`packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts` gave its injected fault a wall-clock budget of about 200 ms (200 polls × 1 ms). On a loaded runner — sixteen UT workers plus coverage instrumentation — the fault lands later than that, the helper falls through to `assert.fail("Timed out waiting for local fault injection")`, and the `UT` job turns the only required status check red on a pull request that does not touch this package. Two pull requests were blocked by exactly this identity on 2026-11-04.

## What was wrong

```ts
async function waitFor(predicate: () => boolean) {
  for (let i = 0; i < 200; i++) { if (predicate()) return; await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1)); }
  assert.fail("Timed out waiting for local fault injection");
}
```

The budget is a fixed count of sleeps, so any event-loop delay counts against it. The product behaviour was never wrong; the wait was.

## What changed

The helper now waits on a deadline instead of a fixed budget:

```ts
const FAULT_OBSERVATION_DEADLINE_MS = 10_000;
async function waitFor(predicate: () => boolean, timeoutMs = FAULT_OBSERVATION_DEADLINE_MS) {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) { if (predicate()) return; await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1)); }
  assert.fail("Timed out waiting for local fault injection");
}
```

The poll interval stays 1 ms, so a healthy run is as fast as before; a loaded run waits for the observation up to 10 s; a genuinely missing fault still fails, and the new test pins that it fails quickly rather than hanging the layer. The failure message is unchanged, so a real regression keeps the same identity.

This touches only the test file — no product code, no other test, and the three existing `waitFor` call sites are unchanged.

## Red first

Commit `731bc426` adds the regression test only, on the old helper:

```ts
let observed = false;
const timer = setTimeout(() => { observed = true; }, 500);
try { await waitFor(() => observed); } finally { clearTimeout(timer); }
```

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/source-health.test.ts
ok 1 - 429 cooldown rejects later agent rounds without another upstream request or wait
not ok 2 - the fault wait tolerates a loaded runner instead of a 200 ms budget
  error: 'Timed out waiting for local fault injection'
ok 3 - parallel 429 callers share cooldown, drain their queue and do not retry inside one slot
...
# tests 17
# pass 16
# fail 1
```

A 500 ms observation is a stand-in for a busy runner: it is the same event-loop delay the ci hit, only deterministic, so the failure reproduces without needing a loaded machine.

## After the fix

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/source-health.test.ts
# tests 17
# pass 17
# fail 0
```

The new test also asserts the fail-fast path after the fix, so widening the deadline cannot hide a missing fault:

```ts
await assert.rejects(() => waitFor(() => false, 50), /Timed out waiting for local fault injection/);
```

Diffstat against `main` `2908e9e8`:

```
 packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts | 17 +++++++++++++++--
 1 file changed, 15 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
```

Commits: `731bc426` test (red), `07c82091` fix.

Ran:
- `cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/source-health.test.ts` — `# pass 16 # fail 1` on the red commit (`not ok 2`, `Timed out waiting for local fault injection`), `# pass 17 # fail 0` on the fix.
- `tsc -p packages/data-source/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — exit 0.

Not run:
- `pnpm ci:ut` (the whole layer, 6 281 cases) was not run locally; CI runs it on this pull request, and the fix is confined to one UT file.
- `pnpm ci:st` / `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run: the change is a test helper, not product behaviour.

## Release

Release category: `release:test` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer with write access — this fork has `pull` only).

User impact: none directly. A flaky UT identity that could turn the required check red on unrelated pull requests now waits for the observation it was already waiting for, so it stops blocking merges it has nothing to do with.

Fixes #918

`GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests` gained two cases in `#915` that assert the walk stays *quiet*: a generated workspace file is not reported, and a file removed between the listing and the read is skipped. Both assert a negative, so nothing in the suite would fail if the walk stopped reporting anything at all — a future narrowing of `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` or `_files` could silence the boundary check while every test stayed green.

This adds the positive half: a file the walk *should* report is reported.

## Why

The two existing cases are `assertNotIn`, so they pass for any walk that returns an empty list. The only test that pins the positive direction is `ArchitectureBoundaryTests.test_node_and_browser_sources_use_only_product_names`, and it asserts the *absence* of findings on the real tree — it cannot go red when the walk is narrowed either, because the tree happens to be clean. A walk that silently ignores `services/api` would keep the entire module green, and vendor naming could escape the boundary unnoticed.

The new case reuses the mocking shape of the removed-after-listing case at `:162`: patch `_files` and let the patched listing hand the walk a path. It differs in what the listing returns — a file that still exists, with a vendor token in it.

## What changed

One test, `services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py` only. No product code.

```python
self.probe = self.API_ROOT / "src" / f"probe-boundary-{os.getpid()}.ts"
self.addCleanup(self.probe.unlink, missing_ok=True)
self.probe.write_text("// deerflow vendor token\n", encoding="utf-8")
original = _files

def only_the_probe(root: Path):
    # Keep the real listing (so IGNORED_DIRECTORIES still governs) and drop
    # every other file, so the assertion cannot depend on the working tree.
    if root == self.API_ROOT:
        return (path for path in original(root) if path == self.probe)
    return original(root)

with mock.patch.object(sys.modules[__name__], "_files", only_the_probe):
    failures = _node_boundary_failures()
self.assertIn(f"content: {self.relative_probe()}", failures)
```

`only_the_probe` delegates to the real `_files`, so the ignore rules still decide what is listed; it only drops unrelated files so the assertion does not depend on whatever else is in the working tree. If `services/api` is ever added to `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES`, the real listing yields nothing and the case fails.

## Red first

Temporarily add `services/api` to the walk's ignore set — the equivalent of a future narrowing that the two negative cases cannot see:

```diff
-IGNORED_DIRECTORIES = {"__pycache__", ".tmp", "dist", "node_modules"}
+IGNORED_DIRECTORIES = {"__pycache__", ".tmp", "dist", "node_modules", "api"}
```

```
$ python3 -m unittest discover -s services/gateway/tests -p 'test_architecture_boundaries.py'
....F.
======================================================================
FAIL: test_a_vendor_reference_outside_a_generated_workspace_is_still_reported
  (test_architecture_boundaries.GeneratedWorkspaceBoundaryTests)
The cases above only prove the walk stays quiet; this proves it still speaks.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../services/gateway/tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py", line 200,
  in test_a_vendor_reference_outside_a_generated_workspace_is_still_reported
    self.assertIn(f"content: {self.relative_probe()}", failures)
AssertionError: 'content: services/api/src/probe-boundary-5.ts' not found in []

----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 6 tests in 0.885s

FAILED (failures=1)
```

The other five tests stayed green under the same mutation, which is exactly the gap: only the new case noticed.

## After reverting the mutation

```
$ python3 -m unittest discover -s services/gateway/tests -p 'test_architecture_boundaries.py'
......
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 6 tests in 1.271s

OK
```

Diffstat against `main` `2908e9e8`:

```

 1 file changed, 23 insertions(+)
```

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s services/gateway/tests -p 'test_architecture_boundaries.py'` — `Ran 6 tests ... OK` on the branch; `FAILED (failures=1)` with the assertion excerpt above under the temporary `IGNORED_DIRECTORIES` narrowing, then `OK` again after reverting it.
- The probe file is created under `services/api/src/` and removed by `addCleanup`, so the working tree is clean after the run (`git status --porcelain` empty).

Not run:
- `pnpm gateway:test` (the whole `services/gateway/tests` discovery) was not run locally; only this module was, and CI runs the full discovery.
- No UT/ST/E2E layers: the change is one gateway test, no product code.

## Release

Fixes #935

The Specialist settings pane prints "Internal server error" for ordinary client mistakes: a name that is already taken, an id that no longer exists, an edit of a read-only built-in. The three routes forward the store's plain `Error`s straight to the catch-all, whose classifier recognises none of those messages, so every rejection becomes a 500. The neighbouring MCP-servers surface already answers these shapes — 400 for a rejected input, 404 for a missing id — and so do the model, provider, proxy-server, project and permission-grant routes, so the Specialist routes were the outlier rather than the norm.

## What changed

`services/api/src/http/index.ts` only, in the block the three Specialist handlers occupy:

- `POST /api/specialists`, `PUT /api/specialists/:id` and `DELETE /api/specialists/:id` now run through `answerSpecialistRoute`, which keeps the store's message verbatim and picks the status from `specialistErrorStatus`:
  - `Specialist not found` → `404`;
  - the store's own rejections → `400` — `Specialist name already exists`, `Specialist skills|connectors are unavailable…`, `Built-in specialists are read-only…`, and the messages the shared classifier already recognises (`is required`, `must`, `cannot`, …);
  - anything else → rethrown to the catch-all, so a genuine internal fault still reads `500` instead of being relabelled as client input.
- `readJson` is still evaluated before the guarded call, so a malformed body keeps the 400 the classifier gives it.

Untouched, as the issue requires: `services/api/src/store.ts` (its wording is the message the pane shows), `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` (held by the in-flight length-rejection fix), and `apps/web` (the client prints whatever the server says).

Commit `3a3c9de4` adds the route test only, against the unfixed server. Six cases: the four rejected shapes fail, the two regression cases (the built-in `enabled` toggle answering 200, deleting a built-in answering 400) already pass.

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/specialists-http.test.ts
not ok 1 - a taken Specialist name is a 400 that keeps the store's wording

    a duplicate name is client input, not a server fault

not ok 2 - an unknown Specialist id on PUT is a 404       500 !== 404
not ok 3 - an unknown Specialist id on DELETE is a 404    500 !== 404
not ok 4 - editing a built-in Specialist is a 400 …       500 !== 400
# tests 6
# pass 2
# fail 4

# tests 8
# pass 8
# fail 0
```

The two extra cases are the "must not regress" half of the acceptance, and both were checked to bite:

- **an unexpected fault is still a 500.** The store has no injection seam (`ApiServerDependencies` exposes `webProvider`, `connectorFetch`, `fetchModelCatalog`, `fetchUsageExchangeRate`, `ideaTreeRepository`, `mcpTransport`, `remoteCompute` — no store), so the test fails the HTTPS response itself from inside the guarded block: the injected throw must reach the catch-all as `500 Internal server error`, not be claimed as a 400. Making the route relabel every fault as 400 (the naive fix) turns exactly this case red and nothing else.
- **the status mapping is pinned directly** on `specialistErrorStatus`: 404 for the not-found message, 400 for each store rejection, and no status at all for `Catalog database is not initialized`, `database is locked` and `ENOTDIR: not a directory`.

```

{"status":"FAIL","planned":6389,"executed":6389,"passed":6385,"failed":4,"skipped":0}

940.author: zhaochen39
940.body:
Research runs configured with `reasoning_effort: low` could lose that setting on the Evolve/search path and be snapshotted as `high`; long calls could also fail on transient upstream errors. This change carries the Run's thinking mode and effort through Evolve, preserves the existing `high` default only when no effort is supplied, and streams model completions with bounded retry, deadline, and stop handling. 941.body:
Fixes #937

## What happens

`#932` classifies any message matching `/\bis too long\b/i` as client input, and the dispatch at
`services/api/src/http/index.ts:3938` answers a classified error `400` **with its text**. Two
executor messages contain the phrase mid-sentence and embed a filesystem path, so with `#932`'s
pattern they answered `400 {"error":"Runner bundle path is too long for tar: /…"}` instead of
`500 {"error":"Internal server error"}` — before `#932` both were 500 and the path stayed hidden.

## Change

One pattern, at `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts:37`:

```diff
-/\bis too long\b/i,
+/\bis too long\.?\s*$/i,
```

Anchored at the end of the message, so only a message that *ends* with the phrase is client input.
Between the phrase and the end this allows exactly two things: an optional sentence period (`\.?`)
and trailing whitespace (`\s*`), which is what copy that ends with `is too long.`, `is too long\n` or
`is too long. \r\n` needs.

Why this shape and not something looser:

- **Not `\b…\b` (#932's unanchored form).** Any mid-sentence mention would classify, and the two
  executor faults (`packages/executor/src/runner-bundle.ts:76,80`,
  `packages/executor/src/remote-compute.ts:777`) put the phrase in the middle of a sentence that
  carries an absolute path — the client would get `400` with that path in the body.
- **`\.?` plus `\s*$`, not `.*$`.** The only tolerated trailing characters are the sentence
  terminator and whitespace. `… is too long for tar: <path>` still has text after the phrase, so it
  stays a fault, and a path can never appear in the `400` body. The same holds for
  `… is too long for a Unix socket: <path>`.

Nothing else changes: no new code, no change to the limits, no change to a throw site.

## Tests

`services/api/src/http/error-classification.test.ts`:

- the eight legitimate length messages pinned **by name** (not by count), including
  `pip indexUrl is too long` (`packages/schema/src/environment.ts:393`), which the first draft of
  #937 missed;
- the two executor messages as **negative** assertions: they must not become client input. The
  runner-bundle fixture spells its path `/srv/ws_a/data/model.bin` — a neutral absolute path, not the
  CI builder's home. This test file ships inside the release payload, and
  `scripts/binary-release/build-payload.sh` (`assert_no_build_paths`) rejects any payload file carrying
  the builder's own `HOME`; the merge-queue run `42148873426` failed `Binary release (x86_64)` and
  `(aarch64)` on exactly that literal. The sentence shape the case pins (a length phrase followed
  mid-sentence by an absolute path) is unchanged;
- the existing negatives stay: `Chunk length 16384 exceeds the internal buffer budget` and
  `Database invariant failed` are still faults;
- three **shape** probes, one test each so a regression names the shape it dropped — trailing
  newline (`"The LLM API token is too long\n"`), trailing period (`"The LLM API token is too long."`)
  and period-plus-CRLF (`"The Neo4j password is too long. \r\n"`) — all expected `true`.

## Red first

Two red runs, in this order, both before the code they pin.

**1. The anchor itself.** With the product pattern reverted to `#932`'s unanchored `/\bis too long\b/i`
and the by-name test kept, the run before the anchor commit was:

```
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/http/error-classification.test.ts
not ok 2 - a length rejection ends with the phrase, so a path-bearing executor fault stays a fault
  error: |-
    Runner bundle path is too long for tar: /home/runner/work/ws_a/data/model.bin
    true !== false
# tests 2
# pass 1
# fail 1
```

**2. The terminator.** On the anchored tip `60e36dbe` (`/\bis too long$/i`), the three shape probes
were added with the product pattern untouched, and all three went red on `false !== true`:

```
not ok 3 - a length rejection survives a trailing newline
not ok 4 - a length rejection survives a trailing period
not ok 5 - a length rejection survives a trailing period and CRLF
# tests 5
# pass 2
# fail 3
```

After `\.?\s*$`: `# tests 5 / # pass 5 / # fail 0`. Per message, `#932` pattern → this tip (probe
importing both modules; the probe is not committed):

```
true  -> true   The LLM API token is too long
true  -> true   The proxy URL is too long
true  -> true   neo4jHttp is too long
true  -> true   neo4jUser is too long
true  -> true   The Neo4j password is too long
true  -> true   Model ID is too long
true  -> true   The stored runnerToken is too long
true  -> true   pip indexUrl is too long
true  -> false  Runner bundle path is too long for tar: /srv/ws_a/data/model.bin
true  -> false  The remote data directory path is too long for a Unix socket: /tmp/sc-remote/ws_a/.agent.sock
false -> false  Chunk length 16384 exceeds the internal buffer budget
false -> false  Database invariant failed
```

And the three shapes, previous tip `is too long$` → this tip `is too long\.?\s*$`:

```
false -> true   "The LLM API token is too long\n"
false -> true   "The LLM API token is too long."
false -> true   "The Neo4j password is too long. \r\n"
```

## Relation to #932

`#937` is the follow-up Security filed on `#932`, and `#932` must not be re-tipped for it. The shipped
change is therefore self-contained: this PR introduces the phrase with its own terminator handling
(`/\bis too long\.?\s*$/i`), so it does not depend on `#932` merging, and `#932`'s branch stays
untouched at `8b4c124c`. `#932`'s pattern is the input this PR narrows from, and the red run above
uses exactly that pattern, so the readings stay comparable. If `#932` lands first, this PR reduces on
rebase to the `\b` → `\.?\s*$` change on the line `#932` introduces, plus the test.

## Reads

Tip `08fc9b7694f03b746f1f332df9d66053aa6503f9` (tree `f37490d96a`), branch
`dev/937-bug-the-is-too-long-client-error-pattern`, base `main` `e4c206d1`. Diff vs `main`: 2 files,
+58/−0 (test +50, product +8).

Ran:

- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/http/error-classification.test.ts` —
  `# tests 2 / # pass 1 / # fail 1` with `#932`'s pattern (first red); `# tests 5 / # pass 2 / # fail 3`
  with the shape probes against `is too long$` (second red); `# tests 5 / # pass 5 / # fail 0` at this
  tip.
- the payload path scan, applied to the file the binary-release job flagged, with the same
  boundary-anchored `grep -rIlE` shape and needles `build-payload.sh` uses: no match for
  `/home/runner`, `/home/xuke` or `/home/`; the only match is the fixture's neutral `/srv/…` path,
  which is not a needle.
- `cd services/api && npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0 (product; the package config
  excludes `*.test.ts` from the build).
- `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p .local/tsconfig.937.json --noEmit` — exit 0; a probe config extending
  `tsconfig.tests.json` with `types: ["node"]`, including only
  `services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` and its test.
- `git diff --numstat upstream/main..HEAD` — `45 0` test, `8 0` product.
- `node --import tsx .local/probe-937.mts` — the per-message table above, `#932`'s module against this
  tip's module.
- `grep -rn "is too long" --include=*.ts packages services` — the eight legitimate throw sites all
  end with the phrase; the only mid-sentence ones are the two executor throws.
  `packages/model/src/client.ts:279-281` also lists `input is too long` / `prompt is too long`, but those
  are markers for `isModelInputTooLargeError`, a different classifier that additionally requires a
  400/413/422 status.

Not run:

- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` (root) in this worktree: it fails on unrelated packages
  because `packages/feedback-worker` has no `node_modules/@sciencediscovery` link here
  (`TS2307 @sciencediscovery/operational-logging/feedback`); the probe config above type-checks the
  changed files with the same settings.
- `pnpm ci:ut` / `ci:st` / the E2E layers — CI runs them on this PR.
- A route-level HTTP probe on this head. The dispatch line is unchanged and the classifier is its
  only input; `#932` already carries route-level 400 readings for the same path.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` — two pathological executor failures keep the generic 500 instead of
echoing a filesystem path, while the eight length rejections and their punctuated/newline-terminated
variants still answer 400 with their message.

The label itself needs repository write access, which this fork does not have, so a maintainer has to
apply `release:fix`.
