943.author: HugoXK
943.body:
Fixes #942

## What happens

In the feedback dialog one multi-select of 10 screenshots attaches 8 (the cap in
`packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts:40`) and says nothing at all: no error, no hint, no count.
`prepareFeedbackImages` left the loop silently, `result.error` stayed `undefined`, so the
`feedback-inline-error` line in `FeedbackDialog.tsx` rendered nothing. The two dropped files were lost
without a word, and the user submitted believing all 10 were attached.

The function's own comment promised the opposite ("stops at the first failure so the dialog can show
the reason instead of silently dropping the rest"): it stopped on failure, but the cap — the far more
common path — dropped the remainder silently.

## Change

Three files, and `apps/web` only.

1. `apps/web/src/feedback-images.ts` — `prepareFeedbackImages` now returns `skipped: number` next to
   `images` (and `error`, unchanged). A pick that does not fit the cap is counted instead of dropped:
   the loop turns the old `break` into a `continue` that counts, so every file still costs no decode.
   This is purely additive: `images` and `error` keep exactly the semantics they had, and an image
   that fails type/decode/size still returns early with its error.
2. `apps/web/src/FeedbackDialog.tsx` — the dialog holds `skippedImages` next to `images` and renders
   one neutral hint (`feedback-hint`, `role="status"`) naming the cap and the count:
   `Only the first 8 screenshots were attached; 2 skipped.` It is **not** the `imageError` slot: that
   slot is keyed by `ImagePrepareError` and describes an image that failed, while this one explains a
   partially successful pick. The count is cleared when the dialog reopens, after a successful
   submit, and when a thumbnail is removed — it always describes the newest pick.
3. `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` — `feedback.images.truncated` in both locales.

The English copy is number-neutral on purpose. The issue's suggested wording
(`…; {skipped} were skipped`) is `1 were skipped` at `skipped: 1`, so this PR uses the number-neutral
`{skipped} skipped` instead: `Only the first {max} screenshots were attached; {skipped} skipped.` reads
correctly for every count, and the Chinese wording (`只附加了前 {max} 张截图，另有 {skipped} 张被跳过。`)
already was.

## Tests

New `apps/web/tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx` (6 tests). The four acceptance directions, all driven
through a mounted `FeedbackDialog` and its real hidden file input, with only the browser pieces
(`createImageBitmap`, canvas `toBlob`, `FileReader`) stubbed:

1. **at the cap** — pick 10: 8 thumbnails, notice
   `Only the first 8 screenshots were attached; 2 skipped.`
2. **under the cap** — pick 2: 2 thumbnails, no notice at all;
3. **remove then pick** — pick 10 (8 attached), remove one (7 left), pick 2: 8 thumbnails and the
   notice says `1 skipped` — the count describes the newest pick, not the previous one;
4. **both locales** — the zh-CN dialog renders `只附加了前 8 张截图，另有 2 张被跳过。`

Two unit tests keep the pure return value pinned: `skipped === 2` for 10 picks at the cap and
`skipped === 0` for 2 picks under it.

Not covered (coverage boundary, not defects — the code paths exist and behave as written, no test drives
them; follow-up tests are tracked separately, not in this PR): the notice disappears immediately when a
thumbnail is removed (`FeedbackDialog.tsx:323`); an image failure and the truncation notice can render
together when one pick both drops images at the cap and fails one (`:484`/`:488`); reopening the dialog
and a successful submit each reset the count (`:163`/`:288`); and picking once more while already at 8
yields `0 added, 1 skipped`.

## Red first

**1. The missing signal.** Test first, product code untouched, on base `9871f2dd`:

```
$ cd apps/web && ./node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx
not ok 1 - ten picks at the eight-image cap report the two that were skipped
    undefined !== 2
not ok 2 - two picks under the cap report nothing skipped
    undefined !== 0
# tests 2
# pass 0
# fail 2
```

`images.length` was already 8 and 2, so the failing half is exactly the absence of a truncation
signal.

**2. The missing notice.** With the `FeedbackDialog.tsx` change reverted and `skipped` still returned,
the dialog tests fail where the user-visible behaviour is missing:

```
ok 1 - ten picks at the eight-image cap report the two that were skipped
ok 2 - two picks under the cap report nothing skipped
not ok 3 - the dialog names the cap and the dropped count after an over-cap pick
ok 4 - the dialog says nothing extra while every pick fits
not ok 5 - removing a thumbnail frees a slot for exactly one more pick
not ok 6 - the Chinese dialog carries the same notice with its own wording and numbers
# tests 6
# pass 3
# fail 3
```

Test 4 passing there is the point of the test: nothing extra may appear while everything fits.

After both halves: `# tests 6 / # pass 6 / # fail 0`.

## Reads

Tip `8ebaedfabf447a0c23770899f8a87133029c7b7f` (tree `2ce76c1f7a`), branch
`dev1/fix/942-feedback-image-truncation`, base `main` `9871f2dd`. Diff vs `main`: 4 files, +278/−5
(`feedback-images.ts` +11/−5, `FeedbackDialog.tsx` +14, `messages.ts` +2, new test +251).

Ran:

- `cd apps/web && ./node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx` —
  `# tests 2 / # pass 0 / # fail 2` red first, `# tests 6 / # pass 6 / # fail 0` at the tip.
- `cd apps/web && ./node_modules/.bin/tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` (the package's own
  `test` script) — `# tests 1250 / # pass 1250 / # fail 0`.
- `cd apps/web && ./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0.
- Rendered-state check: the dialog tests assert the thumbnails, the notice text and its absence
  through `react-test-renderer` on the real component; the hint uses the existing neutral
  `feedback-hint` style and `role="status"`, so it is announced but not styled as an error.

Not run:

- `./.local/typecheck-app-tests.sh apps/web/tests/FeedbackImages.test.tsx` — the probe reports the same
  pre-existing noise every `react-test-renderer` test in this repo produces (`TS2591` for
  `node:assert/strict` without `types: ["node"]`, `TS7016` with no `@types/react-test-renderer`), and
  no gate type-checks `apps/web/tests` (`apps/web/tsconfig.json` includes only `src/**` and
  `vite.config.ts`). Verified by running the same probe on `apps/web/tests/ComputeReadiness.test.tsx`
  and `apps/web/tests/ConfigurationRequestCard.test.tsx` on the base tree: they fail the same way.
- A browser-level E2E journey for the feedback dialog — none exists in the repo for this dialog, and
  the component test above drives the real handler.
- `pnpm ci:ut` / `ci:st` / the E2E layers — CI runs them on this PR.

## Scope

`apps/desktop/src/feedback/feedback-images.ts:116` carries a copy of this function with the same
silent cap drop, and its own dialog has the same gap. This change is the `apps/web` face only; the
desktop copy is left untouched and needs the same fix, tracked separately.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` — the feedback dialog now names the eight-image cap and the number of
screenshots it dropped instead of losing them silently.

The label itself needs repository write access, which this fork does not have, so a maintainer has to
apply `release:fix`.

944.author: zhaozhaozz
944.body:
Nightly and release real E2E runs showed only a gate line, so a reader could not see how each selected case finished. This publishes one per-case execution table for `profile: daily` and `profile: release`. Merge and pull-request profiles do not publish it. The slice summary, the non-gating PUCT review table, and the Biomni suite report stay as they are.

## Case execution table

The combined real E2E accounting job writes the table into its job summary, into the run artifact `case-execution-details.md`, and into the existing `real-e2e-results` artifact as `dashboard-summary.json`. Nightly appends that same Markdown to the outcome summary next to the existing gate line. A release run uses the same real E2E workflow, so its accounting summary and artifact carry the table too.

Columns, in order: `#`, `case`, `status`, `score`, `peak memory GB`, `generated tokens`, `judge tokens`, `total tokens`, `tool calls`, `duration min`.

`#` starts at 1. Rows with `started_at` come first, oldest first. Selected cases with no `started_at` follow, ordered by case id. Every selected case is one row, including failed and unfinished cases.

`score` uses `evaluation.overall_score`, then `evaluation.total_score`, then `evaluation.score`. It does not use the non-gating PUCT review score or `evaluation.race.overall_score`. `duration min` is `generation_duration_ms / 60000`, to one decimal place. Generated tokens are the generator's recorded completion tokens. When a usage record has only a total, that total is shown and the split is `n/a`. Token counts of at least 1000 use a compact form (`34.2K`, `14.5M`); smaller counts stay integers. A missing measurement is the text `n/a`. A recorded zero stays zero. A missing optional cell does not change the gate verdict. The required check name `merge-gate` and the ruleset are unchanged.

The table and `dashboard-summary.json` copy only these identity and numeric cells. Prompts, answers, traces, assertion text, error strings, and secrets are not copied.

`dashboard-summary.json` keeps the existing count fields (`tests`, `passed`, `failed`, `skipped`, `flaky`, with the last four summing to `tests`) and may add an optional `table`. The producer writes the final display strings, including `n/a` and compact token counts. A summary without `table` remains counts-only. Any consumer that already reads `dashboard-summary.json` from a test-results artifact can render `table` from the declared columns, without a repository-specific parser.

## Validation

On `27ae924c95f4a4a8867b78915fb8e8ec391f05cc`:

- `node --test .ci/case-execution.test.mjs`: 5 passed, 0 failed. This covers the header and column order, `started_at` ordering, `n/a` for a missing metric, inclusion of a failed case and an unfinished case, score precedence, and exclusion of a planted secret and model text from the Markdown and the summary. It also checks that `merge` and `pr` write neither file, and that the workflow steps run only for `daily` and `release`.
- `pnpm ci:selftest`: 123 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: planned 4, executed 4, passed 4, failed 0, skipped 0.
- `pnpm docs:check`: passed, 0 lint problems.

The self-test, L1, and docs check ran on this commit before it was pushed. This review re-ran the case-execution contract test on the same commit. No paid real-model daily or release run was dispatched, so this pull request does not yet include a live GitHub Actions log of the new table.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable. This change only publishes CI evidence: a job summary, a Markdown artifact, and fields inside `dashboard-summary.json`. It does not change a product page, API, CLI, runner, or which cases execute, and it adds no user-visible product path. The contract test above is the check for the new table.

## Release

Release category: release:internal

User impact: none for product users. Nightly and release run summaries gain a per-case execution table.

Compatibility and migration: none. `merge-gate` is unchanged. Summaries that omit `table` parse as they do today.

Fixes #850

947.author: moShangLouTou
947.body:
Desktop's system Skill switches wrote the active project's selection, while JiuwenSwarm maintained its own global switches and task startup could overwrite them. Desktop now reads and updates JiuwenSwarm directly, including its built-in and locally installed skills. The reporter completed functional testing and confirmed that the switches survive restart.

Closes #896 (reporter-approved Desktop/JiuwenSwarm scope).

## Behavior

- Individual and bulk switches use JiuwenSwarm's persisted global state without a project requirement. Built-in/local skills use the existing name endpoint; ScienceDiscovery packages use a by-id endpoint that imports on first enable. Sources are labeled and same-named skills stay distinct.
- Task startup never rewrites the global switches. Globally disabled ScienceDiscovery skills are filtered before fallback readers, resource readers and skill-dependent tools are registered. A failed global-state read stops the skill-enabled run; a failed package import cannot change global switches.
- Bulk operations continue after individual failures and display the backend's saved state with the failed skill names.
- Existing JiuwenSwarm skills retain their stored state. Unimported ScienceDiscovery packages stay unavailable until explicitly enabled; Desktop-created packages are enabled immediately. Changes apply to newly started tasks, without promising live changes to an in-flight task.

## Validation

Final candidate: `c7b1bf9ffae28130c7843d10ad12718001fa5236`, rebased onto `face1d4046daa92dab0c295716e88c0902abddb9`. Executor environment: Linux/WSL x86_64, Node 22.19.0, pnpm 11.1.2.

| Final-head check | Executed | Passed | Failed / skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Targeted JiuwenSwarm agent regressions | 8 | 8 | 0 / 0 |
| First-import / disable / re-enable API route, mocked adapter | 1 | 1 | 0 / 0 |
| Desktop Skill API-client unit cases | 3 | 3 | 0 / 0 |
| Desktop Chromium UI journeys, mocked API | 3 | 3 | 0 / 0 |

API and Desktop typechecks and `git diff --check` passed. The first post-rebase browser attempt was stopped because the updated main branch required an unbuilt feedback-client export; after building `@sciencediscovery/operational-logging`, the same three UI journeys passed. Per the reporter's explicit request, validation remained limited to lightweight related checks; full local L1/UT/ST/E2E slices were not run. Remote required checks remain applicable.

Commands:

```sh
cd services/api
node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern='global|globally|desktop|could not install|skills are installed|SKILLS=ours' src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts
node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern='desktop skill switches import' src/server.test.ts
cd ../../apps/desktop
node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern='skills' tests/api-settings.test.ts
cd ../..
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck
node test/sync-e2e.mjs --check
PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$PWD/.e2e/browsers" apps/desktop/e2e/node_modules/.bin/playwright test --config apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts settings-interactions.spec.ts --grep 'JiuwenSwarm built-in and local|same-named skills|refused built-in' --workers=1 --retries=0
```

## User journeys and limits

Automated UI journeys passed: toggle built-in/local skills with no ScienceDiscovery catalog and reload; operate same-named skills independently and in bulk; preserve saved states and show a refused built-in switch. The API regression passed first import followed by disable/re-enable. Agent tests reject a direct `read_skill` bridge call for a globally disabled skill and verify no startup switch writes.

Reporter-run acceptance: before this main-branch rebase, the reporter explicitly confirmed normal product behavior and persistence after restart; the exact installed build and runtime flags were not supplied. No step counts or execution logs were supplied, so this is user-reported evidence rather than an independently observed live-backend run. Native Windows/macOS, alternate skill/tool modes, and live specialist/subagent or two-project execution-trace matrices were not independently run. Web settings redesign is outside the agreed scope.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (label pending maintainer permission).
User impact: Desktop Skill switches control the executor's global availability, including built-ins, and persist across restart.
Compatibility and migration: no settings migration; existing JiuwenSwarm switches remain authoritative.

The title over the conversation is printed from the open Session's own
record, while the sidebar already followed a rename the moment it happened. A
Session's first message is named by the service ahead of the run, on the stream
the app is already reading, so the row appeared with the message and the bar
kept saying 未命名会话 for as long as the answer streamed. Renaming from the
row's menu or from the bar itself had the same lag: the write reached the list,
and the bar kept the old name until the Session was reopened.

Fixes #957.

## Take the name from the evidence already in hand

`session.updated` carries the renamed Session, and the rename route's reply
carries it too. Both are merged into the open `detail`, so the bar and the row
print the same name at the same moment. Messages are preserved by the merge,
and no extra request is made: the event is the service saying the title
changed, which arrives end-to-end earlier than the read-back that follows the
run.

## Never fold a replayed record over a newer one

The stream a run is followed on replays from cursor 0, so opening a Session
whose run is still going delivers its earlier `session.updated` again — older
than the record `openSession` has just read. Folding it would put the bar back
under the name from before the user's own rename, and the composer back under
the approval mode and the expert it had then, until the run ended: the same
bar/row disagreement this PR removes, reached by leaving the Session and coming
back.

Every write on the service stamps `updatedAt` (`store.updateSession`,
`compareAndSetSessionTitle`, the approval-mode and expert writes), so the merge
now takes the newer record whatever order the two arrive in
(`apps/desktop/src/app/use-workspace.ts:983`). A record of the same age is the
same state and may land. The merge also lands in the cache that paints a
Session on the way back to it, so the older title is not shown while the read
is in flight.

The regression journey seeds exactly that: a live run whose log holds the
record written before the rename, a rename from the bar, a switch to another
Session and back. Held open until the page is being looked at, the replay has
provably reached it when the assertions run.

## Screenshots

Before is the merge base `face1d40`; after is this branch. Both are the same
mocked workspace running the same journey — the bar over the conversation and
the sidebar row that must agree with it.

**Rename from the bar — zh-CN**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![rename zh before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/3c4f6ab76c6b279ea9254658d50e7bcc3cb97935/docs/pr/session-title-sync/before-zh-CN-rename.png) | ![rename zh after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/3c4f6ab76c6b279ea9254658d50e7bcc3cb97935/docs/pr/session-title-sync/after-zh-CN-rename.png) |

**Rename from the bar — en**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![rename en before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/3c4f6ab76c6b279ea9254658d50e7bcc3cb97935/docs/pr/session-title-sync/before-en-rename.png) | ![rename en after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/3c4f6ab76c6b279ea9254658d50e7bcc3cb97935/docs/pr/session-title-sync/after-en-rename.png) |

**The first message names the Session — zh-CN**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![first message zh before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/3c4f6ab76c6b279ea9254658d50e7bcc3cb97935/docs/pr/session-title-sync/before-zh-CN-first-message.png) | ![first message zh after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/3c4f6ab76c6b279ea9254658d50e7bcc3cb97935/docs/pr/session-title-sync/after-zh-CN-first-message.png) |

**The first message names the Session — en**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![first message en before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/3c4f6ab76c6b279ea9254658d50e7bcc3cb97935/docs/pr/session-title-sync/before-en-first-message.png) | ![first message en after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/3c4f6ab76c6b279ea9254658d50e7bcc3cb97935/docs/pr/session-title-sync/after-en-first-message.png) |

In the "before" images the sidebar row already carries the new name while the
bar over the conversation still prints the old one (`晶体结构分析` /
`Untitled session`) — the defect. The run's read-back is held open for the
seconds the capture takes, which is the window the defect lived in.

## Test entry: hold one route's answer

The mock that answers `/api/**` for the desktop browser entry can hold a
matching route's answer until the spec releases it. That is what lets the new
journeys look at the bar while the run's read-back is still outstanding — the
window the defect lived in, and one that no assertion on final state can see.

It also answers the run-events route as a stream to a caller that subscribes
(`accept: text/event-stream`) and as JSON to the one rebuilding a finished run,
because the replay that the second new journey is about only happens on the
subscribed path.

## Validation

Baseline `7057aaf6`: the two original assertions fail with the old name still
in the bar (`晶体结构分析` and `未命名会话`). With the freshness gate removed
from this branch, the third journey fails the same way at
`sessions.spec.ts:246`, so it pins the replayed-record case rather than
passing for its own reasons.

Candidate, head `4b11b27f` on `main` at `face1d40`:

- Desktop unit tests: 744 passed / 0 failed.
- Desktop browser E2E (L2 mocked entry, `apps/desktop/e2e`): 105 passed /
  0 failed — includes the three regression journeys below.
- `pnpm typecheck` (desktop): exit 0.
- CI run `42178875479` on this head: policy, L1, UT, Coverage and all five
  mocked E2E shards pass. ST reports 50/51 — one case in
  `services/api/src/configuration/p1-runtime.integration.test.ts`
  (`model.repair_credential`) answered `Run not found` once; it passes 12/12
  four times in a row on this head locally through the tagged runner, and the
  same file passed in the ST job of the previous head. merge-gate fails only
  on that ST result (`CI gate failed: st: failure`).

Earlier heads on this branch ran the same layers: L1 4/4, UT 6403/6390 passed
with 13 failures, ST 50/51, mocked browser E2E 126/133. The 13 UT and 1 ST
failures reproduce unchanged on an unmodified worktree of `main` and are
host-side:

- `services/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts` — this host's bubblewrap 0.6.1
  has no `--disable-userns`.
- `services/launcher/src/serve.test.ts` (5) and
  `services/launcher/src/source-evolve.test.ts` (5) — the owned services these
  tests start exit before becoming healthy here.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts` — the recorded
  trajectory of a JiuwenSwarm turn.
- `scripts/start-stack-lock.test.mjs` — the harness' own pre-fix body restored
  anyway.
- `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` (ST) — the pinned Python runtime comes
  from GitHub Releases and exceeds that journey's five-minute download budget
  from this host.

The 7 mocked E2E failures on the earlier head were all `apps/web` journeys;
three reproduce identically on unmodified `main` (two font-metric layout
ceilings on this host, and one blocked on a micromamba download), and the other
four pass on both trees when re-run. This diff touches only `apps/desktop`.

## E2E user journeys

PASS — tested SHA `4b11b27f`. Browser, desktop L2 mocked entry:

| Scenario | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rename a Session from the bar (double-click the title) | Row and bar both show the new name at once; the write survives a reload | PASS |
| Send the first message in a new Session while the run's read-back is held open | Row and bar both show the name the service published ahead of the run; 未命名会话 does not linger | PASS |
| Rename, switch to another Session and back while a run is going, then release the run's replay | The replayed `session.updated` arrives and changes neither the name in the bar nor the composer's permission mode | PASS |

Command: `playwright test --config apps/desktop/e2e/playwright.config.ts`
(105 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped).

The desktop L2 entry mocks every `/api/**` response; the real-stack journey
(`apps/desktop/e2e-real`, tier L3) is unchanged by this front-end state fix and
was not part of this verification.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: the conversation's title updates at the same moment as its
sidebar row, including the automatic name taken from a first message, and a
return to a Session that is still running no longer shows the name it had
before it was renamed.
Compatibility and migration: none.

The `release:fix` label cannot be applied from this fork (the account has no
write access to the upstream repository); the label is pending a maintainer.

951.author: zhaochen39
951.body:
The shared tagged plan selects only `status:reviewed` cases, so the eleven Playwright specs that had not been audited against the E2E-META contract sat in a `legacy` project that CI never ran. Their cases matched no profile: they stayed in the catalog but were never executed by the PR, nightly or release plans, and reported zero. That is the case-level coverage gap this issue records for the browser layer. This pull request moves those specs onto the shared plan and removes the quarantine path, so there is no second way to run them.

## Every migrated spec declares its contract

All eleven specs now carry an E2E-META block, install the mocked network guard, and, where a journey needs a model, register loopback OpenAI-compatible stubs (`test/support/stub-models.ts`) for the hanging and slow profiles the Stop and queue journeys need. Their 41 identities are `status:reviewed`, so the shared e2e slice selects them; no case from these specs sits outside every profile anymore. The stub helper owns the HTTP context it cleans up with, clears the global default model when it created it, deletes the Sessions that still reference the profile, and reports a failed deletion instead of swallowing it, so a run leaves no profile pointing at a closed loopback port. `node test/check-e2e-meta.mjs` reports no errors.

## Narrow and mobile coverage is kept

`apps/web/src/styles/responsive.css` implements dedicated ≤1024 px (off-canvas sidebar), ≤900 px (stacked conversation/workspace, folded settings) and ≤600 px (full-width dialogs) layouts, and the frontend guidance asks reviewers to inspect narrow and low-height states. The migrated journeys therefore keep their viewport matrices instead of dropping them:

- `issue-37-composer-height` measures the empty, capped, capped+2 chip and capped+6 chip states at 1366×768, 1440×900 and 1920×1080, plus a 500/600 px sanity case and a 1280×640/1366×640 low-height scenario.
- `issue-143-proxy-settings` and `gateway-token-recovery` keep their 390×844 cases; `issue-44-session-stop` S4 and `agent-run-componentization` S1 keep their mobile viewport steps.

## One way to run the browser suite

With no spec left to quarantine, the `legacy` Playwright project, the `ci:e2e:legacy` script, `test:legacy` and `test:legacy:list`, `CI_ALLOW_LEGACY`, and the legacy branches of `.ci/run-e2e.sh` and `.ci/test-catalog.mjs` are gone. The shared plan and `pnpm ci:e2e` are the only entry points, and a spec that declares neither `@mocked` nor `@real` is collected but not run. No workflow, required check name or shard layout changes: the CI contract change is the case selection inside `.ci/`, not the merge gate.

## Two state defects the journeys surfaced

- Switching or deleting a Project now drops the Session selected in the Project being left (`apps/web/src/App.tsx`). Without it, scope-aware consumers paired the new Project with the old Session and rejected the request while the new list resolved.
- Escape inside the proxy URL guide now dismisses only the guide (`apps/web/src/ProxySettingsEditor.tsx`); it no longer propagates to the System configuration dialog underneath. The proxy journey asserts the dialog stays open and usable after Escape.

## Validation

- `pnpm test:list --slice e2e` freezes the plan at 174 identities for profile `pr`; the eleven migrated specs contribute 41 of them.
- L1: planned 4 / executed 4 / passed 4.
- UT: planned 6383 / executed 6383 / passed 6379 / failed 4. The four are load-sensitive timeouts in files this branch does not touch: two cases of `packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts` ("Timed out waiting for local fault injection"), one of `services/runner/src/execution-manager.test.ts` ("Execution did not reach expected state within 30000ms") and one of `services/runner/src/server.test.ts`. Run on their own, those three files pass 16/16 and 82/82. Upstream `main` at `e4c206d1` passes `UT` in CI (run 42161416462).
- ST: planned 51 / executed 51 / passed 50 / failed 1. `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` downloads the pinned CPython standalone build from GitHub, and the download was terminated after 300 s on this host. `ST` is green on `main` in the same CI run.
- E2E: the full suite ran at planned 170 / executed 170 before the four restored journeys were added; the five failures are the `journey-*` cases listed below, which this branch does not touch. Every one of the 41 migrated identities was then re-run on the final tree and passes 41/41 (issue-37 8, issue-143 3, issue-44 5 + 2, session-run 1 + 1, agent-run-componentization 6, e2e-auth 9, gateway-token-recovery 3, subagent-rename-and-align 2, timeouts-runtime-status-user 1).
- `.ci` self-tests: 118 tests, 0 failed. Shared-plan self-tests (`pnpm test:tagged:selftest`, with `SCIENCE_TEST_PYTHON` pointing at a managed environment): 63 tests, 0 failed.
- `node test/check-e2e-meta.mjs`: 88 spec files, 0 errors.

## E2E user journeys

PASS for every journey this pull request adds or changes. Tested tree: `1070aeda`, the single commit this pull request contains; the branch merges cleanly with `main` at `e4c206d1`. Browser: Playwright Chromium against the local stack; all model calls go to loopback stubs, no real model or external service is contacted.

- Run the migrated journeys from the shared plan: the plan selects the 41 reviewed identities, all 41 execute, and all 41 pass. → Expected: every migrated journey is planned and executed. → Actual: PASS.
- Session Stop and queue isolation (hanging model, session A blocked while session B runs, repeated Stop, mobile viewport): Stop stays reachable, both sessions stay independent, no refresh is needed. → PASS (7 journeys).
- Composer at 1366×768, 1440×900 and 1920×1080, at 500/600 px, and at 1280×640: the message area keeps at least 55% of the viewport in the idle and running states, at least a third when the composer is capped or carrying chips, no chip row that fits clips a pill, and send stays clickable inside the composer. → PASS (8 journeys).
- Proxy URL guide: keyboard Escape closes the guide; the System configuration dialog remains open and usable. → PASS.
- Narrow viewports: the proxy settings dialog and its URL guide fit a 390×844 screen without horizontal overflow, and gateway token recovery and the agent-run componentization flow keep their mobile steps. → PASS.
- Project switch and delete: the Session selected in the old Project is cleared before the new Project's list resolves. Exercised by the migration journeys; no dedicated assertion is added, because the guard prevents an in-flight mismatched request while the visible end state is the same without it, so a browser-level journey would not fail if the guard were removed.

The other five failures in the same run belong to `journey-*` specs this branch does not touch. Two depend on this host's font metrics (a paragraph measure of 774 px against a 760 px limit in `journey-artifact-viewer-large-screen`, and 601.23 px against 580 in `journey-model-connect-wizard`); the two `journey-error-diagnostics` cases expect a Session that the local stack does not seed; `journey-prepare-environment` is BLOCKED because the managed Python base reports `micromamba setup failed`. `main` at `e4c206d1` runs all five mocked E2E shards green.

Commands: `pnpm test:list --slice e2e`; `pnpm ci:e2e`.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`
User impact: no new capability. The browser suite now runs where it previously reported zero, and the two state-handling defects above are fixed.
Compatibility and migration: developer-facing only. Remove local use of `ci:e2e:legacy`, `test:legacy`, `test:legacy:list`, `CI_ALLOW_LEGACY` and the `legacy` Playwright project; run `pnpm ci:e2e` (shared plan) instead.

Part of #817.

## Summary

Evolution kept expanding after a candidate already met the goal score because both engines kept a per-rollout `solved_threshold` of `2.0` and never passed a search-level target. This wires the scorecard's `solvedThreshold` into `evolve` / `async_evolve` as `target_reward`, and reports that stop as the goal being met (not shortfall / expansion cap).

Fixes #948

## Changes

- Pass scorecard `solvedThreshold` as `target_reward` into both evolve engines
- Keep per-rollout `solved_threshold` at `2.0` (avoids rollout skip)
- Surface `target_reward` stop as goal met in UI/API messaging
- Tests: narrow related cases + regression for stop-on-target

Tip: `769d565b`

959.author: ink999107
959.body:
## What this fixes

Two `settle`s can overlap. `send` clears `running` **before** it awaits `settle` (`use-workspace.ts:1141-1144`), so the composer is usable again while a settle's three reads — `getSession` → `listRuns` → `buildReplays` (which may re-read run events one by one) — are still in flight. The next message's turn can then end and start a second settle before the first one lands.

The older settle wrote its stale snapshot unconditionally:

- `commitReplays(target, batch)` replaced the session's replay cache with an older, shorter list. Its internal `replayEpoch` is only bumped by `clearSession`, not per settle.
- `rememberBounded(detailsBySession, target, fresh)` replaced the first-screen cache with the older transcript.
- `setDetail(fresh)` put the older transcript on screen, hiding the newer message and its answer until the next turn — and moving the design anchor back to the previous design, which reopens the auto-continue stall path fixed by F9/F12.

Reproduction: send a message in a long session (slow `getSession`) or the first turn after a refresh (`buildReplays` re-reading run events), and have the next message's stream fail/end quickly. The second settle lands first, the first lands last.

## The fix

`apps/desktop/src/app/use-workspace.ts`, two changes:

1. New `settleEpoch`, incremented by every `settle`. Each settle asks at each write whether it is still the newest one (`newest()`), so the decision is made when the write happens, not when the reads started. The three writes above are gated by it. `sendEpoch` continues to guard the pending message and `resetRun`; `refreshSessionLists` / `refreshPanel` stay unconditional because a stale settle's refresh is still a refresh.
2. `clearSession` bumps `settleEpoch` as well. `openSession` calls `clearSession()` and then sets `sessionRef`; leaving A and reopening A before an A-settle lands would otherwise make that settle look current again even though its reads describe the left Session. This mirrors the existing `replayEpoch` handling.

No changes to `follow`, `openSession`, `buildReplays`, or `replayEpoch`'s existing uses.

## Test

New `apps/desktop/tests/workspace-settle-order.test.ts` (sibling of `workspace-settle.test.ts`, same harness): both turns end at once, so both sends start a settle; the newer settle lands first with `[FIRST, SECOND, ANSWER]`, then the older one lands with `[FIRST]`. The assertion is that the transcript stays `[FIRST, SECOND, ANSWER]`.

Red first, on the unmodified source:

```
not ok 1 - a settle that lands after a newer one does not put its older transcript back
  error: |-
    the older settle did not write
    + actual - expected

      [
        '/evolve-design --algorithm puct 一',
    -   '/evolve-design --algorithm puct 二',
    -   'answer 2'
      ]
```

Green after the fix:

```
$ npx tsx --test tests/workspace-settle-order.test.ts
# pass 1
# fail 0
```

Full suite and typecheck in `apps/desktop` with the fix:

```
$ npm test
# tests 821
# pass 821
# fail 0

$ npm run typecheck
(clean)
```

## Relation to #814

This is the last finding (F13) from the #814 review, where it was confirmed but left out of that PR so its approvals would not be invalidated. **#814 is not touched** (it has since merged); this PR is based on `main`.

Not merged manually — CI + committer approval as usual.

959.title: fix(desktop): let only the newest settle write what it read
